why.quote: An elective course is any four-unit English Department course.
why.reasoning: The catalog's fixed list leaves out many four-unit English courses (e.g. the 180 series, 162, 172, 117F, R17, freshman seminars, additional sections of 190). The list is now every fixed 4-unit ENGLISH course below 200 in the catalog, plus the catalog's own list. It excludes R1A/R1B and the 45 series, as the FAQ (https://english.berkeley.edu/undergraduate/major-requirements/faqs) says: 'The only 4 unit classes that do not count as electives would be 45 series courses, or any R1A/R1B courses.' The FAQ also says 'in the instances when you take N166 (the Department's Summer Study Abroad Course which is 6 units) ... both courses can be counted towards the major', so ENGLISH N166 is included. Two catalog entries are dropped because they aren't four-unit English Department courses: ENGLISH 84A (a 2-unit sophomore seminar) and ENGIN 184 (another department). Variable-unit independent/group study (98, 99, 198, 199) is left out; the department treats those separately ('non-typical electives').
